analysis.name: Dr. Aman Sunder

review_highlights.comment: expects you to spend 70 dollars on a textbook if you want higher than an 80 on any exam, even if you memorize the powerpoints he puts on elc down to the wire. I do not think this content should be hard at ALL but he puts questions on the exam that are literally un answerable unless you have studied the texbook or happen to make a lucky guess.

This professor does not teach. Instead, course material is locked behind a textbook paywall. Lectures are low effort AI slop. Exams are lockdown browser with camera. Dr. Sunder sends out passive aggressive emails to the entire class, and is not afraid to accuse students of cheating. Do not waste your money or time on this course.

Absolutely egregious class. AI videos, textbook, slide decks with mistakes in them. Insanely passive aggressive rude emails and very flippant attitude to students. Who hurt you dude?? 60 question exams. webcam and lockdown browser, 100 question final. says that nowhere in the syllabus. Do not take.

NOT an easy A. Tests are so difficult for no reason- You have to remember so many specific facts from slides and lockdown browser with webcam. Class taught through AI videos, so you basically have to learn everything on your own. No help from the professor, who barely contributes to the class.

Class is entirely reading textbook chapters with AI lecture videos. Exams are lockdown browser with camera which was fine but the rude/passive aggressive emails chewing the class out for how bad they did on the exams really isn't necessary. Don't take if you're looking for an easy online class to fulfill a credit.

analysis.name: Ashley Nichols
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would not recommend unless she is the last option available. She writes the hardest tests by far of any section (All the profs are different), and the highest class average for the semester on all three tests was an 81. She also will tell u to email her with questions and then proceed to say "Well go over it in class, and then never go over it".

All you have to do is show up to class+pay attention. Her lectures are interesting and she's funny, so the material just kind of sticks in your brain. Don't buy the textbook! There are 11 open note quizzes. Your grade is made up primarily of tests but as long as you make flashcards and learn them, the exams are exactly what she says in class.

GREAT professor (very friendly and funny). Grade is mainly based off exams but if you know how to study you can easily get As. Study the key terms and rules in DETAIL (highly recommend making a big quizlet). Attendance is for extra credit only. Don't bother buying the textbook all test content is from lectures.Lowest midterm grade replaced by final

Love her, she's so engaging and is so passionate about LEGL as she was an attorney herself. 5 grades in the grade book, 3 are midterms, one the final, and one is the average of hw quizzes, so each 20% which can be tricky if you bomb an exam. In class, she goes over the content and not many practice problems like on the exam so know content well.

Professor Nichols is funny, her lectures are really interesting, and she loves participation. There isn't a lot of homework for the class but exams are extremely difficult in comparison to what you learn in class. Attendance isn't mandatory and you can gain a whole 1 (one) point for extra credit if you aren't absent for more than 6 classes.

analysis.name: Norris Armstrong
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 303 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Armstrong's portion of Genetics was AWFUL. Seriously, you can study weeks for the exam, yet when you get to the exam you will be wondering if you are taking the correct test because it is NOTHING like what you did in class. Test averages were in the 50's. I was so terrified of failing and not graduating. Hands down hardest class for my bio degree.

Dr. Armstrong is a very respectable professor. He knows the material he is teaching very well. My negative aspects of having him were really just the level of difficulty of the exams. Some of that is strictly due to the material we were learning at the time, but his exams are something you have to put SERIOUS commitment into in order to pass.
Dr. Armstrong was not nearly as hard as people make him out to be. As long as you know the lectures well you should do fine on the exam. He gives plenty of practice material before the exams too.

I prefer lectures. In the beginning he lectured more, but then it became more about doing worksheets in designated groups for half the class that I could do at home. You don't have to buy a textbook for his class. Class is mostly mandatory. As long as you have 80% in-class participation on TopHat, you get the full 100% for that grade.

Armstrong is a nice guy, & he is def willing to help if you go to office hours. His lectures don't have all the info on the slides do you do have to go to lecture and take notes. There are 5 exams (75% of ur grade and no drops). Exams are based on your ability to apply lecture material not just memorize genetics. Practice problems help a TON!

analysis.name: Alex Asay
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 141 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He is very friendly and a very interesting person. He doesn't have the typical “professor distance” and feels easy to approach. The class content itself is engaging to me, sometimes he starts with an interesting question to lead into the topic of the day. There is not a heavy workload, and he assigns a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Prof Asay is an amazing philosophy professor! There are two short texts required for the course, and he makes them as easy to understand as possible. He gives lots of extra credit opportunities, really wants you to get an A. Easy short quizzes (5qs) due before each class, one easy midterm, and a final that isn't required if you have an A. Take him!

The best professor I have ever had. His class was attendance-mandatory, but if you show up and do the reading/quiz online, you will pass the class. He gave so much extra credit, which helps a lot. He is also a very easy grader and is super cool. Had the midterm, and he gave the study guide; everything that was on the study guide was on the midterm.

Alex is an incredible professor! He meets college students where they are and makes learning so much fun! Philosophy can be a tough subject, but by using real life experiences and incorporating the lives of each student in the class he makes the subject more clear. This class reminded me that a classroom does not have to be confined by four walls.

Very chill and funny professor. You are allowed 6 absences without penalty (as of Spring 2026), but there are tons of extra credit opportunities if you accidentally pass this, like attending outside speakers and lectures to cancel out absences. Also, the class is chill and not too bad, just participate a LITTLE in class and you are chilling.

analysis.name: Audrey Haynes
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 444 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: If you take her online then good news: everything is open book/note! Yes, some of the questions can be difficult, but if you read the chapter and did the study guide you're pretty much set. The only videos you are REQUIRED to watch are a few that you have quizzes on. Lectures are optional, or if you just want to skim the slides she has that too.

Professor Haynes was the best professor I've had here so far. She doesn't just want you to pass her tests, she wants you to learn the material and really apply it. She's even inspired me to minor in Political Science. You will have to read the book, but the info is relevant so it isn't terrible. Online quizzes every week can be a grade booster too.

Dr. Haynes is very approachable/understanding if you ever need to speak with her. The textbook is very dense so ATTEND LECTURE because her powerpoints break up a lot of the info you need to know. Tests are not easy but quite fair if you go over the readings/activities she assigns. Breakouts are pointless but mandatory. Overall a good experience :)

I enjoyed taking Dr. Haynes's class online! Her assignments require a lot of critical thinking, and if you're ever stuck or need feedback on an assignment, she's more than happy to help you. Her assignments aren't hard, but make sure not to fall behind! Also, she offers a good amount of extra credit if you ever need a little boost!

Dr. Haynes is hands down one of the best professors at UGA. If I had the chance I would take every class she offered. She is one of the most caring and involved professors I have ever had and I highly recommend taking any of her classes. Attendance is required but you will want to be there.

analysis.name: Adam Wineland
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This man is awesome. He would stay and help try to explain. However, he would teach us the long way of doing something instead of the shortcut. There's not a lot of work in this class besides tests and quizzes. However, the midterms are not worth a lot. The quizzes are take-home. He gives practice tests for the midterms which were included.

Professor Wineland is great. Attendance is not mandatory and everything is available online so I never had to show up to class past a certain point. If you have any questions he is helpful and readily available. Great class, could not recommend more if you are an independent learner.

Professor Wineland understands his students, plain and simple. He doesn't lecture or stand in front of the class, but he gives enough explanatory material that it really doesn't matter. You only have to go if you have questions, and if you do, he will very clearly answer it. His class will definitely strengthen CAD skills without stressing you out.

HIGHLY RECCOMEND this class! Professor Wineland is super nice, quick to answer questions, and is very helpful. Grade is made up of 5 projects, each with 2 progress checks (basically easy 100s) and a quiz (unlimited tries), no final exam. I had no prior auto cad experience so the first project was a learning curve but I promise it gets a lot easier.

Definitely take his class, he's an amazing professor and knows what he's doing. There's about 5 projects in his class and weekly assignments to track your progress. While you can do everything 100% online he has in person classes everyday so you can go in if you need help with anything. But If you stay on top of your assignments you'll be fine!

analysis.name: Allison Howard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: ADORE Dr Howard. She is genuinely the coolest! This course was harder than any of my other psych classes at UGA so definitely be prepared to study for exams, but she is an incredible professor, so I still highly recommend the class. Tests are a mix of MC, matching, and free response. She has participation grades sporadically, so go to class.

I would take her class again and again. It is so well organized, and she genuinely cares about her students. The topic in itself was also very interesting to me. I always studied the night before and did very well on all her exams. You can also drop the final. If you're looking for a good psyc class to fill a requirement, this is the one.

I will genuinely miss Dr. Howard and her class. It was very interesting especially when the class participates. Exams were completely fair; study flashcards and definitions, and HW she gives (which is weekly, and reasonable, and helpful). Has one book that you read, it was really good! One assignment on it, which was a zoom. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

I absolutely adore Professor Howard. Her criteria and syllabus are straightforward: 3 exams make up the majority of your grade, with the remaining small percentage coming from homework via TopHat and in-class participation. The final replaces your lowest exam grade, so if you are satisfied with your grade, the final isn't needed. Slides are key!

Dr. Howard is my favorite professor I have probably ever had. She is so kind and really cares about the stuff she teaches. Take this class- it is not too hard, so if you put in effort and study well, you'll get a high grade. I will actually miss her. Tests and assignments are very fair, she does not trick you; take this class & if you love animals!

analysis.name: Abigail  Steiner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 91 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She was very caring & such a sweet person! The tests are made by department so they're the same no matter the professor, my only flaw is the exam problems were harder than what we went over in class but overall not terrible. Accounting sucks, just make sure to practice & study a lot to understand the concepts!

1st and 3rd exam were really hard, 2nd was cake. The 1st exam I could do the class problems and review she gave super well, but the exam was way harder. For the 3rd exam I could do all her review, class notes, and the online homework perfectly, but the exam was totally different. Class is useless but required. GET SKOOLERS. I regret not doing it.

Very nice professor, but that only goes so far. So many surprises on the exams, despite studying many hours and feeling confident heading in. She does not prepare you well for the exams at all, go ahead and preorder skoolers.

Grading isn't as bad as previous semesters, b/c of more extra credit now. Tests aren't comparable to quizzes and in-class problems, much harder and weigh a lot. Final is cumulative. Says will give partial credit for workout problems, but gives none unless you go to office hours. Steiner is really nice though and learns everyone's names and cares.

Professor Steiner is amazing! She cares so much for her students and is always offering a ton of resources to study with for tests. She is willing to answer any questions you may have. She even has a different class event each semester! Ultimately, the professor you have will not really affect your grade that much, but Steiner is an amazing choice!

analysis.name: Mark Abbe
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Abbe is an amazing teacher, and it is very clear that he comes to class genuinely excited to talk about what we are learning. He is also always ready to answer questions after class or during his office hours. This course is exclusively lectures and his slides have almost no words on them (only pictures) so good grades depend on showing up.

Professor Abbe is very caring and clearly passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are detailed and interesting, but the class is graded by very few things and the exams are very difficult and graded by TAs, who tend to be inconsistent. Honors section essays are helpful for this but one bad exam grade and you can't fix your grade.

DO NOT TAKE!! Took this course to fulfill req (not related to my major)& thought it wouldn't be too bad based off other ratings here but it was genuinely awful. I worked the hardest/most on this class just to barely get an A. Grading is by TA's and is inconsistent, tons of unrelated textbook homework's that take 20-60 min, 3 tests + attendance.

I really enjoyed Professor Abbe's lectures, and it's easy to tell that he genuinely enjoys teaching. I have to complain about the grading. The TAs are responsible for grading the exams, and it depends on which one you get. I received a low grade on my first exam, took the feedback given to improve for the next exam, and got around the same grade.

Took this to fulfill a world lang/culture credit and ended up spending more time on this class than anything actually relevant to my major. Tests are completely written, no MCQ, must study for 5+ hours to get just a B. Online assignments take FOREVER. Only plus is that attendance is taken with a written sign-in sheet, so your friends can cover you.

analysis.name: Amrit Tiwana
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved professor Tiwana! He made a usually boring topic truly interesting and by applying the topics to real world scenarios/relevance I felt like I was learning really important things. His lectures were really engaging/entertaining. Study the lecture slides for the tests and pay attention in class and you'll be fine for tests. Take his class!!

This was the best course to take out of all of the flex core options for MIS majors. It is a fascinating course that gives you a great understanding of the IT world. Dr. Tiwana is the goat. He is hilarious and has so many funny stories to tell while lecturing. He says he cold calls but he barely did. Group project was easy. Take him if you can!

Dr. Tiwana is genuinely the best professor I've ever had. The class was so interesting and I learned so much about the business world because he always talked about current news, which I loved. If you can take his class, DO IT! He will teach you so much & is also a really fair grader! Exams weren't too bad but some questions were confusing.

Dr. Tiwana is the best professor I have had in Terry. Absolutely incredible at conveying complex topics in a digestible manner. He is incredibly engaging -- class was a joy. I would take him for literally any class.

Dr. Tiwana is such a great professor, one of the best I've ever had. His lectures are always relevant to what's happening in the real world and he's super engaging. He also has a great sense of humor and is very knowledgeable. You will not regret taking his class.

analysis.name: Brent Shuman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loveee this class! The content is super interesting and Dr. Shuman is very nice. There are exams every other week but it's actually way better than 4 big exams because the volume of content on each exam is way less and the whole system is way less stressful. I would totally recommend Dr. Shuman and the honors sections of this class!

Dr. Shuman is great! Knows his stuff but his slides can be confusing and a little disorganized. If you take notes and use the resources he provides tho, you'll be fine. Exams every 2 weeks, but loved it cause they had less content, lots of bonus questions, and mostly MC. Seriously, such a manageable course! Heads up, he is a pretty slow grader...

I was really scared to take Shuman because so many people say that you're going to fail if you don't take Lemon, but I was pleasantly surprised! He's pretty approachable and willing to work with your schedule if you need to take the test on another date or something. Tests are definitely difficult but he's pretty fair about grading.

Dr. Shuman is a good lecturer, very nice/approachable. His part of the class was definitely more difficult than Armstrong's, but i'm not sure how much of that was his fault. As long as you are confident in your ability to do the practice problems that he gives for exam prep you should do good on the exam.

Dr. Shuman is nice overall, his lectures were interesting and helpful. The criteria for the exams was pretty clear, and I'd say they were similar difficulty to Armstrong's. The practice problems and learning objectives given in eLC are enough to be able to do well on the exams.

analysis.name: Benjamin  Cooley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 318 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He is a bad intro-to-physics professor. It took a month to grade the first test, and the average was a 55. We got a 20-point curve, but I still didn't pass. The second test isn't graded yet, and the drop deadline is tomorrow. Scienceguyz wasn't helpful because of his teaching style. Good luck!.

Not an easy A. You will not slide by and pass. You have to work hard and put time in to this course. Will be a challenge, but will teach you valuable lessons on how to be successful in future Physics classes, like finding a good group to study with, using offices hours and actually talking to your teacher when stuck, and coming to class prepared.

AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!! I have all A's as a junior exercise science major and have never failed an exam in my whole life. I failed the first exam even (avg was a 50) after getting science guyz and weeks of studying. He takes forever to grade and gives problems that are not proportional to the level of the class (Intro to Physics). No extra credit.

Mr Cooley was not cool. His lectures were really boring and extremely irrelevant. He went great depth into giving you real world examples and talking about the why. That did not prepare you for the given homework assignments or the tests. His class involves using 3 different websites to go on a journey and they do cost money.

I usually don't rely heavily on course ratings since some reviews reflect course difficulty rather than teaching quality. However, in this case, I genuinely believe the learning experience would be improved with a different professor. He is a nice guy, but his teaching style and tests don't match up. I don't recommend Dr. Cooley.

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bhan is hard but not difficult. I feel like students have forgotten that they are in college and that not everything is going to be given to them in a platter. Even if you go to class everyday, prepare to put a substantial amount of work outside of class. Read the textbook, do the homework, and do her practice questions. You'll be fine!

In class I felt that I understood the lectures, but Swati is the most difficult professor I have ever had. Be prepared to have at least 6-10 hours of homework per week. But don't worry the homework is useless when preparing for the tests as the tests are comprised of problems you have never seen before. I highly recommend taking Christensen.
I attended very class, made a 100 on every homework assignment, went to tutoring regularly, and still failed every test. Good luck.

I have never worked so hard in my life to get such a poor grade. I spent hours upon hours studying, reading, preparing, doing practice. The assignments are easy to follow and are great for learning, but the tests completely blindsided me. She sets up questions deliberately to trick you. She's also very condescending in emails when you ask questions

Professor Bhan's lectures are interesting and engaging and she's really funny in a nerdy accounting sense. She is very available after class and with her office hours. At the beginning of the semester, she provides a study plan. If you follow this, you should get  an A. Students often blame their poor grades on Swati but it's never her fault.

review_highlights.comment: She tag teams the class with Dr. Ryman. If you are a traditional learner, or learn better on your own, you will HATE this class. Most of the material is presented in a flipped-classroom way and majority of class is spent on questions that have nothing to do with tested material or long tangents. You will have to learn all the material yourself.

I have had Dr. Bush for a few courses now and she's just an okay lecturer. Her explanations never really made sense and I'd just end up more confused at the end, so I just stopped asking questions. While she puts on a front of truly caring for her students, she has little to no grace towards students having to miss class for personal reasons.

I've had Professor Bush for three classes, but this was the first where she was the lead. She focused more on group work and workload management than actual content. Quizzes were only open for 12 hours like they were the Epstein files, and we got almost no test-like practice.

She had great lectures, and she explained things well. However, I dont think she cares as much about students as she tries to make it seem. She told us to talk to her about concerns when potentially changing homework due dates to a day earlier, and when I talked to her about my concern, she blew it off and said she had it harder in college.

Her lectures were a little difficult to follow sometimes due to the amount of images on them, so definitely don't miss class if you can avoid it. A lot of graphics were explained in person and not on the slides they post, but they do post every slide set online. Easy to get in contact with for office hours, and I found that going was helpful

analysis.name: Brian McDonald
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Brian is incredibly sweet and is willing to meet you where you stand. 2 midterms worth 50%, final is 40% and it replaces lowest midterm grade, and hw is 10%. Final grades are curved at the end. Lectures were long, and he placed a huge emphasis on understanding. Incredibly smart guy, but he didn't rly simplify things down in lecture enough for me

While he is a nice and caring professor, his lectures were very difficult to follow. Almost all lectures are about theory with little to no examples to follow. It felt like I had to teach myself the majority of Calc III through the textbook. Despite the tests being hard, he does put a generous curve on them. Overall would avoid if possible.

Professor McDonald isn't too bad. His lectures aren't very straightforward, and he goes on tangents about unnecessary information often. He teaches with proofs and doesn't show many examples with actual numbers. His tests and homework are based on the textbook (free pdf). But he curves your final grade, so it makes up for his teaching style/skills.

Prof McDonald is a well-meaning man, but he has no idea how to teach at all. I've taught myself calc iii from the textbook. His lectures are unfollowable and not even related to what were tested on half the time. This class has been a lot of stress when it really shouldn't be. Also grade breakdown is 10% hw, 25% each tests 1 and 2, and 40% final :/

Dr. McDonald is a very nice, but he really falls short in his teaching. His lectures are mainly proofs rather than teaching you how to do the actual calculus. If you want to teach yourself how to do everything, then take him. If you're expecting him to teach you to do the calculus, don't take him. The exams are also really really hard.

Professor Wyatt is a great guy. He grades very fairly and explains things very well. I would 100% take a class with him again.

Brandon is a very helpful and understanding teacher. He was very sympathetic to our learning process and willing to take extra time to explain concepts we were struggling with. The class was small, so he was able to make certain activities personal to feel more engaging. Great stuff!

Brandon is a wonderful professor, he is very kind and understanding as he isnt that old himself. The course is homework heavy, but that is more a symptom of german department as a whole rather than his own choice. I would take german 2 with him if i could but it is not required for me. Dr. Barnes is great, you'll be incredibly happy with him! Textbook is free, lecture materials posted online, and he's able to teach some more complex topics in a simple and entertaining way. to the guy who gave a 1.0 because he submitted a project late, have you considered that maybe... just maybe, that it's a skill issue? This guy was the goat and the way he explained stuff made it sound so easy, this class was geniunely the easiest course of my life. He is also very organized so that helped alot too.

Having Brad in 1302 really made me start to love computer science. All of the material and reading he gives in the class are very interesting and very helpful. It is a lot of work and is tough but it really does teach you some amazing things and I will take Brad Barnes for any CS course in the future.

First off, Brad got me to switch my major to comp sci almost immediately. He gives a ton of work, so you should make this class the focus of your semester. analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

review_highlights.comment: Truly one of the all-time greats. Chill dude and gives a LOT of extra credit. Exams were easy, HW is reasonable, lectures werent too boring and he clearly is enthusiastic about teaching. Show up and you will get an A, if you are a smart person show up sometimes and youll get an A. Knows all of his students names, sums up the type of guy he is.

One of my favorite and most enjoyable Professors ever! It may take a week to get used to his teaching style, but he has a very clear gift for teaching and explaining concepts effectively. Would 100% recommend if you are in the Honors College.

Prof. Balasubraniam was the kindest prof I've ever had at UGA. Always had a positive attitude and tried his best to engage students in the class. He also tried to make the class as entertaining as possible, frequently making jokes. The HW and tests were exactly what he taught in class and were straightforward. He gives a LOT of extra credit too.

I loved Professor Balasubrbramaniam. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but he will definitely call you out if you never go. He doesn't post much, so you are going to want to be there for pop quizzes and extra credit. He cold-calls. If you take this class and show up, you will get an A. He is so funny and a great professor to write you a rec. Take him!!!

If his section fits your schedule, TAKE SARANGAN FOR THIS CLASS! He does everything possible to make sure we don't get lost in the process during lecture and greatly rewards attendance. Only downside is he doesn't post annotated notes, but he does have office hours, AND it's the type of class you WANT to go to.

analysis.name: Bryan Barber
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

There are only 4 tests which consist of things from the lectures and from the textbook. Lectures are not posted until 2-3 days before the test so going is encouraged

analysis.name: Lyndsay Loomer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Loomer was nothing short of brilliant. With effortless charisma and charm, she kept the whole class engaged from start to finish. Her lectures were not only insightful but paired with PowerPoints so polished and elegant, they felt like a reflection of her own style. The Baccarat Rouge of professors.

THE GOAT. This class is so easy and whenever I went to class (you don't need to lol) it was super informative and she's super engaging. Go through her exam review slides before the exam and you'll do great. Grades are just homework and 3 exams and they're all light. She is awesome I would absolutely recommend her.

I want Dr. Loomer to adopt me she is so motherly and kind. She prides herself on having an easy class. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you do go she is extremely helpful and does a great job breaking the content down. Exams are very straight forward and don't require tons of studying. Would honestly give her higher than a 5 if I could.

Prof. Loomer is amazing! Lectures are super engaging with lots of great examples to help you learn course concepts. If you're attending class and paying attention, you should have zero issue getting the grade you want. Before each exam, she posts the main concepts to know, which are highly representative of the actual exam. Super caring and likable
What hasn't already been said about the GOAT?

analysis.name: Nicholas Llewellyn
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Llewellyn is nice, but the whole chemistry department is just not good. He cares to help you, but sometimes the way he teaches is for people who already understand what is happening. I always end up teaching myself through science guyz, but I have done that for every chemistry class I have taken, so I would not say it is his fault.

Dr.Llewellyn is a great professor and is clearly very knowledgable HOWEVER, I found that his lectures confused me more than they educated me. I recommend that you attend lectures just to answer the tophat questions and study on your own. Ochem is already hard in itself, the over explaining and difficult vocabulary just makes it more unbearable.

Very kind and accessible, but this class is impossible without ScienceGuyz, which seems to be the nature of the beast for all 2211 classes here. Lectures became useless after the 2nd exam because he just went on long tangents about complex information that didn't end up on the tests. If you don't get SG, get free peer tutoring, or use both!!

This course sucks, but it's the department as a whole's fault, not Dr. Llewellyn. He's friendly and responds fast. I didn't learn much in lecture, so I learned most things through Science Guyz. He does TopHat questions regularly in class (credit for answering and accuracy). Overall, he's fine, but it's gonna be rough.

Orgo 2 is going to be a challenge regardless of the professor. What was different about Dr. Llewellyn is the way he taught. Llewellyn verbally explains what he's teaching with little visualization. If that is your cup of tea I highly recommend him. If you do take him, definitely show up to class when he is showing Fisher projections its worth it.

analysis.name: Vera Lee-Schoenfeld
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is so nice and cares for her students. She tries her best to make the content easy, but linguistics is hard in general bc it is so subjective. She gave multiple extra credit opportunities to all students. She grades very particularly and looks for specific wording. Online quizzes and no final.

Not a super hard class but it is A LOT of work. Every week there 1-2 chapters (about 30 pages) of reading, discussion posts, homework, and quizzes. It works fine as filler class to get your elective credit but just know you're signing up for 4-6 hours of work per week. The quizzes and exams aren't really hard and they're open book.

She is super kind and a caring! However, I feel like she could do a little bit more to help with the content and it felt like she was more so teaching to the students who had a heavy linguistics background. Attendance isn't “mandatory” but every assignment is turned in on paper and she won't accept it over email. DO EVERY WRITE UP REVISION

I just finished the online version of this class for a summer term, and it was totally worth it! I could sit down for just a couple hours the day assignments were due and finish all my work for the week. Highly recommend taking this class if you need an extra credit in the WLC area.

She is very kind. If you are confused about a topic, she is happy to help you outside of class. Many times I would email her, confused about a topic or a homework assignment, and she would quickly email back some tip or new insight to help me make more progress. She is very understanding about absences. My favorite professor at UGA so far.

analysis.name: Scott Larson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: My class was a flipped classroom!!! The way he explains things in class can be difficult to follow. Tests are hard. He does not enter grades on time AT ALL. However, if you ask questions and stay engaged in class, he will explain things more easily. Just watch the flipped videos, do the insane amount of homework, and this class is manageable.

He wasn't the best professor; however, it isn't impossible to do well in the class. I typically crammed for his exams and scored high grades. I highly recommend you show as much work as possible since he is generous with partial credit. He doesn't enter grades in eLC, so it's kind of a guessing game in that regard.

Prof. Larson stutters a lot, but I understood the material much more from the way he shows proofs for everything he teaches, and all of the resources that there are available to practice. If you do the workbook and homework, you'll do fine on the quizzes and exams. He's also easily contactable outside of class and will help you reschedule things.

Dr. Larson was a nice guy sometimes stuttered ( a lot ) during lecture. Calc 2 is a hard class and def requires a lot of studying so if you take him do your workbook because the quizzes and exam are based off that. He has a weekly quiz and stopped grading them about 5 weeks in. Did not know my grade till after the final, just do good on midterms.

I expected to have a tough time going into this class after looking at the reviews, but professor Larson did a great job explain concepts and solving practice problems. The class itself is challenging for many students, but he encourages people to ask questions and makes sure you understand the material. He is a lenient grader-- js show any work.

analysis.name: Laramie Lemon
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 85 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She only gives 0.5 percent bonus credit fyi, she also has 75% of the grade as tests with no drops and isn't much help with boring lectures. She's not as easy as people say so focus on the first exams and read very carefully

Dr. Lemon seems nice during lecture, but don't be fooled. Her tests are extremely hard, and she rarely drops questions or gives bonus. There are 5 tests worth 75 percent of your grade, no dropped test. My best advice is to NOT take her. I always made above the exam average and still got an A-. She barely gives any extra credit.

She was really great. She co-taught with Rozario and the class was amazing. Expectations were clearly laid out, no extra credit, but she did have multiple drops. Class wasn't too difficult, definitely need to study and put in the work but making an A is very possible. Make sure you take advantage of the time you have on the homework problem sets.

TAKE DR. LEMON! She is so caring, and she tries to make lectures engaging and easy to understand. She teaches alternating units for this course with Dr. Rozario. If you understand the in class work and problem sets, you'll definitely do well on the tests. Lowest problem set each unit dropped, and the final was the 4th unit exam (so not cumulative).

Dr. Lemon is for real a wonderful professor. The grading is clear and split mainly between problem sets and exams. You can easily receive help and the exams reflect what is learned in the lecture and problem sets. Recommend making study groups to check the problem sets. Make sure to know content well. I would definitely urge you to take this class!

analysis.name: Lisa Townsley
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. T was one of the best math teacher I have had in a while. So many opportunities for round up points, she gives several quizzes but only a handful count, and I love her teaching style. She is very approachable and easy to ask questions. She is lowk old fashioned/strict w/ some of her classroom policies but all in all, I love her.

TAKE DR. T. She is a angel sent from heaven to teach calc 2. She gives really solid lectures that make going to class worth it. Lots of homework, but is necessary to do well in calc 2. Her office hours are great to go to and she responds to emails. Her grading is very fair and she gives partial credit wherever she can.

She teaches very fast and assumes you already know everything. Class time is more for questions not learning. She is also pretty snarky when you ask questions and is passive-aggressive. If you do the practice tests, homework, and unit assignments you will do amazing! He is so nice and energetic. He gives out food and his videos are funny/ interesting.

Mark Werner was hands down one of the best professors I've ever had - not just because he made statistics bearable, but because he actually made it fun. THE BEST. He is literally the sweetest human ever. lectures which consist of him talking nonsense of which "you don't need the details in your notes, but...". Doesn't seem to know how to answer even the simplest questions. Essay grading is very tough, but office hours and asking questions can help mitigate this. 8.5/10 overall.

Very nice person, funny, and definitely knows what he's talking about. Does very well in starting discourse about the books while feeding off of participation. A very, very tough but admittedly fair grader when it comes to essays, but willing to answer questions and provide clarification. Even so, I would take another one of his classes.

Mr. Norris's class was genuinely so fun. He makes it interactive, but not in an annoying way. The friends I made in this class are people that I'm genuinely close with now. Mr. Norris is super chill and understanding. If you get the chance to take a class with him, you absolutely need to.

Overall a good teacher. Just show up to class and pay attention in class and you will be fine. You are mainly graded on a few essays and he is a pretty harsh grader but the other grades in the class aren't bad. There is a lot of reading but he talks about the reading in class a lot so if you pay attention to that you should be okay.

Norris was by far the best and funniest literature professor I've ever had. He clearly wants his students to succeed and understand how to mold literature, and its symbolism, into an argument. analysis.name: Rodney Mauricio
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Lots of people are clowning on him but if you show up to class, actually study the content and don't slack off you'll do very well in this class. One of my favorite classes and favorite professors so far, funny and witty but also very good at explaining the material. Prepare to work really hard for an A but its worth it, really enjoyed his class.

I absolutely loved him and this class, the lectures were really engaging. There's 1 book per exam, but they're actually interesting and topical. 
The exams are really hard and need a lot of studying, but the curves are huge. I got a 76 curved to a 100 for one. 

Rating is low bc no one shows up to lectures/reads the textbook that is the whole exam.

Go to class. Ik attendance isn't mandatory but he is 100% real when he says if you don't go to class then you won't succeed in the class. Theres so much material that isn't uploaded to slides or information about exams that are only given in class. You will not do well if you only use the slides and textbook (trust bc i thought it would work)

So overbearing it's almost impossible to take it with other demanding classes. There's textbook work+video quizzes every week, with a book required to read for each exam. Sure, the lectures are entertaining, but there is no structure in this class. No separation of topics into units and exams are so specific and hard he has to curve every exam.

A lot of bad reviews are from unsatisfied people, but he's not actually that bad of a professor. It's imperative that you don't neglect this class, though. Half your grade is a free A, and expect a 20-ish pt curve on exams. Heavy reading, but I'd say just manage your time wisely. Funny guy though! Class isn't mandatory but you really should go.

Whole bunch of AI slop. She reads off the computer the entire class and probably has no idea what half the words mean. If you get a good TA you'll be fine because they are who grade stuff. Pretty doable but you only get two absences ever. Topics are interesting at first and then it becomes straight AI slop. This class has no value

analysis.name: Neil Bendle

Participation is 45% of your grade, but he gives 5+ opportunities to raise your hand in class and give easy examples and opinions. So passionate about sustainability and sweet!

As a student who HATES participating, this class wasn't that bad. It is scary to hear that participation is 45% of your grade. But, if you go to every class, force yourself to talk every few classes and do all of the tophats you will be fine. I tried my best to speak every class and it just did not happen but I still got an A.

*BUSN3300* Neil is a great professor who is very passionate. Most of the class was discussion and prep for the discussion. There were 3 tests based on slides, but tests were open note & open internet (I dont know of anyone who didnt get an A). HUGE part of the class is attendance and participation so only take him if you're ready to talk.

Neil was truly one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures were very engaging, and you can tell that he puts a lot of care into teaching. We had 3 online tests and one presentation at the end of the year, which wasn't bad. All he asks is that you show up and participate as much as you can. I'd highly recommend him to anyone!

He is greatest! He actually cares about his students and what he is teaching. If you can just simply show up to class and participate, you'll get a good grade (participation is 45% of your grade). Exams are open note and easy.

analysis.name: Nicholas Mallis

review_highlights.comment: THE ABSOLUTE BEST!!! I would take him again and again. Attendance is optional, but sometimes I will go just because I enjoy being there. Tests are in person now, but you get full access to the study guide, which carries you through the whole thing. They are multiple choice and absolute cake. TAKE! HIM!!!!!

Honestly the nicest professor I've had at UGA. The content is not bad and the tests are all open notes. I would recommend going to class, because he gives extra points at the end of the semester for good attendance. Wish all professors at UGA were like Mallis.

Dr. Mallis is insightful, very willing to re-explain topics, and frequently goes over assignments in class. Although attendance isn't required and one could feasibly pass the class by not attending, it is much easier to understand the content and get through the homework/exams quickly by going to class and listening to his example walkthroughs.

He is AWESOME! I took BIOS 2010 in person because my advisor recommended it in person for medical school, and it has been the best class I've ever taken in undergrad. There are 3 tests and a final but one gets dropped. Also, there are 12 HW assignments, and lab assignments but both get two drops. TAKE HIM!!!
Absolute legend!!! Helpful inside and outside of class. Makes Biostatistics very easy to understand and is also a super cool musician as well as one of the best professors ever!

Dr. Ovid was my favorite out of the three professors teaching the class. They are good at explaining information and cared about the students in the class. While their exam was harder than the ones written by Dr. Wells, the content was also fair and all covered in the slides. I am unsure why they get so much hate to be honest. Definitely recommend.

She's great, but I agree that her lectures have so much information not tested on/unecessary. I did better on Ovid's test than Wells, who I feel like has more memorization ?s but Ovid is more application based. As long as you do TopHat, practice worksheets, PLA review you'll be fine. Dr. Ovid is a fine lecturer, but her lectures and worksheets 1) covered a lot of content that wasn't on the exam and 2) put the emphasis on non-exam content. I felt that her lectures and videos did not provide enough detail and that it was difficult to learn the content in enough depth. She interacted well but didn't prepare us well.

Dr. Ovid is a decent professor, but the lectures did not seem to emphasize what was most important for our exam and I felt very unprepared. Tested on exceptions to the rule instead of the actual rule, and super specific aspects of something that we only learned in a broad sense. No dropped tests in VPHY 3100/3107 so just be prepared.

analysis.name: Terrell Orr

review_highlights.comment: Professor Orr is about what you expect from a history educator. He gives pretty good in depth explanations to historical topics (he loves labor movements) and explains it in broader history. His lectures are fun, and he is a funny guy. He has a tendency to move class assignments around which can make it hard if you aren't consistently showing up.

genuinely the goat, he's hilarious and selects great readings. I would take this guy over and over again if I could. On top of a great in-class experience, he's incredibly available and really helped me hone in on what I'm interested in. Everyone I know who's taken him ADORES him and he ranks comfortably in their top 3 professors.

Professor Orr gives easy-to-understand lectures. Reading quizzes and in-class writings are designed to be an easy 90 minimum.

If you are just trying to get your history requirement, take this dude, he is super funny, and going to lectures was very helpful for your grade. analysis.name: Minh Trang Nguyen

VIET 3990 is the EASIEST of all her Viet classes (I have taken VIET 1002 all the way up to VIET 3990) as long as you do what you're supposed to do! Professor Trang met up with us WEEKLY to discuss our readings and discussion logs that would help us with our paper. She was ALWAYS accessible outside of class and did everything to help us!

(3100) Being new, his lectures and feedback were brief and hard to follow, yet the course was well-structured and never ambiguous. He has clearly mastered the material and is helping his students do the same: short quizzes forced me to memorize things I should have remembered ages ago, and homework sets were enlightening; the best I've ever had.

The class itself is not difficult, but his lectures tend to overcomplicate. Weekly quizzes that are one question, though he will tell you the topic the class before so it's important to go to get that info. Midterms and final not difficult, but be prepared to teach yourself most of the concepts. Overall nice guy but not a great prof.

Don't listen to the other reviews, as long as you study you'll get an A or B. Homework which was tedious and did not help on exam or quizzes, but he gives a study guide before the exams telling you what questions are on there. Quizzes once a week and were easy problems related to the topic. His handwriting is hard to read so go to every class.

review_highlights.comment: TAKE THIS PROF. She is a HORRIBLE prof, BUT your grade will thank you. Failed both exams (less than a 50) and still made a B in the class because of the online homework being 40%. The other prof may be better for LEARNING but their grading scales are very test heavy and may affect your GPA poorly. Also never went to class and passed with a B.

Take this as an easy GPA booster, I went 4 times in total (twice during syllabus week, twice for in-class exams) and passed with ease. Just do the homework and online quizzes with the help of ScienceGuyz and you'll be fine, the hardest part is the lab practical. Attendance not mandatory and you're allowed a full sized cheat sheet for exams.

If you want that A and to skip class, take ullrich! No regrets!! Failed both tests and still got an A. Homework + reading "quizzes" are 50% of your grade which is PHENOMENAL. You get a drop test, so I didn't have to take the final. An A is an 87! GAMECHANGER. Never went to class. Labs are 30%, so you have to do kinda well on the lab practical.

Dr. Ullrich's class is a fair teacher. Attendance is not mandatory. You will have 2 midterms and an optional final. I got 50s on exams but did well on the lab which is (30%) of the lecture grade and I did all of my homework and quizzes (40%) of the grade. She also offsets her grading scale so even if you get a 75 in the class that counts as a B.

The class was pretty average. I didn't learn much since the professor mostly reads off the slides, and I relied on those for studying on my own. HW is 40% and reading quizzes are 10%, both on Pearson with the textbook. Tests are only 20%. Take this professor if you just want an easy credit without learning actual physics.

analysis.name: Gokul Vasudevan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment:
Dr. Gokul is an average professor, but his tests are really hard to prepare for. Borderline C-B. Also his handwriting is really hard to read.

Also, we had a mandatory field trip all the way to the GDOT OMAT facility near the Atlanta airport and he couldn't coordinate transportation for the 80 people in the class.

His class is a flipped classroom style which wasn't to bad as you just watch his videos before class and do practice problems in class and can ask him questions. The "final" was a group project where you and your group basically got to come up with whatever you wanted without much restrictions.

Attendance is taken through tophat. Flipped classroom so you watch pre-recorded videos to learn. Videos are walkthroughs not actually teaching so you may need to watch them a few times to really learn. He's there to answer any questions and usually gives good feedback. Very easy class, you can do fine even if you don't really understand anything.

Quizzes are relatively easy, homework can be completed during class, and attendance isn't really required as long as you have your work done. But it is a flipped classroom so if you're looking for amazing lectures you're in the wrong place. Overall, he's probably the easiest and most laid back engineering professor you'll find.

very easy class, flipped classroom but he answers any questions and will double check any submissions for you on the spot if you just ask. the TAs grade most of the assignments but it's mainly just for formatting which only changes in requirements for the different softwares (you learn autoCAD, inventor, and civil 3d)

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Viel-Ruma is very passionate about education. This class is a mix of lectures and in class/group activities. She helps you understand certain teaching strategies by implementing them in the class.

Dr. Viel-Ruma is AMAZING! She is very flexible and caring. The class had a lot of assignments, but they were not too bad. The class was a mixture of lectures and class activities. Class participation was a big part of the grade, but as long as you're in class, you're solid. She is very passionate and a very good teacher!

Dr. Viel-Ruma was an amazing professor! She truly cares about student success. Make sure to attend class everyday because a lot of grades are based on participation and in class assignments. Anyone taking EDSE 4030 should definitely choose her!!

She was my Just Breathe/Yoga first year odyssey professor and she was the besttttt!!!! She was always so understanding and sweet. I had this class at 8 am, but she made it all worth it. Plus, she bought us all Einstein bagels for our last class!

She was the BEST! There was lots of homework, but just try to stay ahead a little bit to ease the pain off of your shoulders. The final project was a good chance to be creative! Would definitely take her again!

review_highlights.comment: Dr. V-Smoot is not a bad professor by any means. Her lectures are straightforward and pulled directly from the textbook and tests are open note open textbook. I know it is not the fault of the professor directly regarding the quality of her assistants; however, they have WAY too much grading power. I had to have several assignments regraded by the prof.

Overall an easy, extremely interesting class. There were no tests. Grades based off of online quizzes (15 mins) each week, a couple of short reading assignments, two very doable projects and assignments for My Virtual Child. Really enjoyed the class, and the professor is understanding, funny, and interested in the subject she teaches.

Dr. Vratanina-Smoot is very kind, but her class is very lecture heavy! Attendance is not required but you do have to go to class on the APA research days! Some of her TA's also grade kind of difficult, but you can appeal your grade if you don't agree with it. Overall, a good course.

V-Smoot, such a kind soul and has been so helpful throughout the class. BUT, this class is completely graded by TAs and honestly they like to play with your grade like it is game of basketball. Terrible. I have had my assignments graded incorrectly multiple times. I am always so confident in my work and am constantly disappointed. A lot of trouble.

Challenging class mainly due to the material. Dr. Vance explains concepts semi-clearly and straightforward, lectures are boring. Grading is fair with bonus opportunities. Homework and quizzes are open note, and a cheat sheet is allowed on the midterm, but you still need to put in work outside of class. Responds to emails and is helpful.

Attendance wasn't mandatory, but you received extra credit by attending. He uses slides that are direct copy and pasted from the textbook. The material isn't very difficult, but he'll explain it in such a way that can be confusing. Overall, it's a doable class taught by him if you put in some extra work.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. He gives the hardest exams out of any professor and there are only 2 but are worth 55% of your grade. His exams
also don't align very well with any of the other activities like quizzes, labs or projects, because he tests rote memory on very specific concepts and definitions more so than actual practical application.
I know all the 1301 teachers have low ratings but trust me from the final grades for each, Vance is the worst.

One of the most knowledgeable professors I met who makes his knowledge easily accessible. Taking his RELI 1008 course makes me want to take more of his courses. Gives good feedback on assignments and shares a lot of outside resources. The classes are what you make of it but every opportunity you want is provided!

This is a great professor to take for an FYOS. He definitely required participation and attendance but it was very manageable. The class was basically just a discussion on our book every week. I really enjoyed his class and he is very knowledgeable on the New Testament!

Dr. Coppins is the man. His knowledge of Mark is unbelievable, and you best bet I will be taking him as many times as I can before I graduate. He is very nice, cares for your learning, and encourages engagement. Lots of readings for this class, but they are very interesting. I got a ton out of this class and can't recommend Dr. Coppins enough.

Lectures and her eLC videos cover different content, so going to class and watching videos is important to succeed.Can't recommend enough!

What I didn't like was how he made us go up and down the rows answering questions. After a certain point it gets boring & it's hard to stay motivated. But,This class is an easy A if you show up and do the homework.

Loved him. He loves music and makes sure that everyone fully understands what he teaches. analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This guy is awesome. He always has very clear grading criteria regarding speeches. The homework is easy, yet clear and straightforward. The types of speeches he assigns are always very fun to research and aren't difficult to give. His feedback is honest and gives you concrete areas to improve as a speaker. I highly recommend him as a professor.

Joey was a great prof! I hate public speaking but Joey made it really painless. He's really laid back and genuinely wants to help you be a better speaker. I had him every Monday so classes were 3 hrs long but he made it great & always let us out early. He truly cares about his students & is really funny! 10/10 recommend!!
Joey is super nice, and genuinely such an understanding professor. He just wants to see you improve, and I really do think I got better at public speaking without being under too much pressure.
Dr. Konrad is genuinely amazing!!!! If you get the chance to take him definitely do. He is so kind and caring and makes class fun. Best professor at UGA!!!!!!

Prof. Konrad is awesome (pretty sure he's also a grad student). Class is super easy, 4 Speeches, 2 Exams, and some TopHat assignments. Grading is super relaxed and the class isn't difficult at all. Definitely go to lectures (graded attendance), but you don't have to show up for most speech days. Speeches are easy and Konrad is honestly really good.

analysis.name: Marianne Koshkaryan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you have ADHD or have trouble reading, I do not recommend this class. There are so many readings, and most of them are extremely dense or written in Early Modern English. I only did well because I spent hours reading & taking notes every week. I gained nothing from the lectures bc she spends most time talking about completely unrelated things.

Dr. Koshkaryan is maybe the funniest person I've ever met. She will always find a way to connect our readings to anecdotes from her life, whether concerning growing up in the Soviet Union or her time as a professor. It seems that it's best to visit her office hours before an exam to know what exactly to study, but she is a pretty lenient grader.

Do not take if you have a choice. Sweet lady who knows her Plato, but you literally cannot understand 1 word she says. The quizzes were based off books that are impossible to interpret without her lectures, but you can't understand the lectures. Also, I think it was also the most boring class I've taken. Take anything else

Marianne is a wonderful woman and a fantastic teacher. Her readings had nothing to do with Modern Philosophy, but I genuinely enjoyed each and every one. She really put me on to some heat, and her tests were super easy. She also grew up in the Soviet Union, so her stories were amazing even if they were off track.

Dr. K is a very nice woman, but she cannot teach. Her lectures are so confusing and there's SO MUCH READING. You don't know what you're being tested on either, unless you go to office hours or email her. 3 quizzes (one dropped) plus a final exam plus attendance grade. I just didn't care, and she didn't make me want to care or try.

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, Kohler should be taken whenever possible, there's not really a reason not to. His resume speaks for itself, but being able to have a successful professional in an academic setting is invaluable. Yes, the class can be difficult and you need to pay attention, but if you're taking a core class just for an easy teacher that's on you.

Kohler is super knowledgeable and constantly references his experiences working at JPM in the 90s. However, he is a bit humdrum and sometimes goes on tangents. Class is difficult to be honest and requires your full attention and studying extra outside of class. Not impossible by any means though.

This class is the hardest finance elective I've taken, but Kohler is the best professor in the department to teach it. Genuinely wants you to succeed. Class is made up of tests including a final, projects, homework and attendance. If you're willing to put in the work, I 100% recommend this class because it's so unique. Kohler is seriously the goat

Best and most experienced professor in the Finance major. Extremely knowledgeable, sharp, and caring about students. His classes might be hard, but if you put in the effort and fully understand the content you'll do good. The only people I know who ever complained about him are either unintelligent or simply uninterested in the class.

Professor Kohler's class is one of the most challenging courses I've ever taken as a sophomore. I had a huge learning curve and self-taught myself a lot of the concepts. The lectures were dull and not particularly engaging. Tests were difficult because of framing effect, typically the conceptual questions. Understand the hw and lectures to do well.

This course was too difficult for an intro-level class. The professor's a nice guy, but how this class is structured is confusing. Class was not difficult at all. Basically the level of a high school science class (fyi if you took ap environmental it is the same content). Professor is so nice and wants to make class engaging. He is super boring and challenging. Many people I know took this class with a dif professor and they did well. His test are in person and rather difficult. I studied for hours and never made above a B on an exam. Group project is easy and will help your grade.

review_highlights.comment: He won an award for his teaching for goodness sake! He's awesome! His lectures and the examples he uses in class are very helpful and the little assignments are actually fun to complete. If you study, the tests aren't bad, although I know some people struggled. There are extra credit opportunities and he has an end of semester party at his house!

Dr. Knox is one of the most caring professors at UGA. He actually cares about students and tries to help them succeed in his class as best he can. Attendance is not mandatory. Tests require lots of studying. Minimal homework assignments due every week. Overall great class, just be prepared to study and put in the work.

Dr. Knox was the best professor I've ever had! He is passionate about his subject and his students. He gives a lot of extra credit and really cares for his students. It isn't an easy class, but he tells you that on the first day. He has great reviews and study guides to make a difficult subject as straight-forward as possible. Would take again!

This class was very difficult and I mostly struggled with the tests. But Knox will go out of his way to make sure you do well, but only if you come to him first. He gives you plenty of opportunities for extra credit, like up to 2.5% added on to your final grade. I wouldn't recommend this class but I would recommend Knox.

Dr. Knox's love for weather is palpable. He made a great effort to engage all the students. The class requires a weekly packback, tophat, and a weather forecasting project (plus midterm and final). By the end of the year he expressed feeling used so I hope he incorporates some new practices to limit this as I don't think it was the students fault.

This is the greatest professor you will ever have. Witty, caring, encouraging and made this the best class I've ever took. Please, please, please take a class with him!

This class is doable but VERY hard. Genti cares a lot about his students and gives extra credit, adjusts grading scales and gives curves but even with these you must try. Exams are difficult but again doable if you prepare well. Can be frustrating but not impossible.

Awesome guy. He really cares about making sure students will succeed in his class. review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kochut is just brilliant, and excels at explaining difficult, abstract concepts to students. Luckily tests were 60%, and a breeze compared to the programming, which was beyond hard.

Dr. Kochut is a super respectable professor with a really interesting and different class. It's a relatively straightforward class and my grade could've probably been higher, however I just wasn't as passionate as I originally thought. There's a few quizzes, in class assignments, two exams, and a handful of projects. Super lenient grader too.

Great professor, doesn't overcomplicate things. The material can take some effort to learn but there are in-class activities to help. He is very nice and will answer any question. He stays up to date with the material. There are 2 projects that you do in pairs. Exams are in-person and closed-notes but he gives clear study guides so just study.

Mobile Dev with Kochut is great. If you pay attention, you will do good. The only gripe I have is that the whole class uses Java for Android. Great to learn the fundamentals, but Kotlin is the real-world modern choice that is easier to write and I wish we would've used that. Also the 2 exams sum up to 50% of the final grade and are not easy.

I was already familiar with the content, so I can't speak for the quality of the lectures. But since I took the class (in-person) over the summer, his lax attendance policy meant I could skip most classes (since I lived an hour away). Also, he was accessible and gave good one-on-one feedback.

The textbook can be found online! ( wish I knew this sooner )
Tests are not often, and they are simple; by the time you take them, you will know everything by heart.
She is truly a natural at lecturing!
Kahoots and prizes, which are so sweet.
Lots of reading guides and podcasts, which are a bit tedious but necessary, I think.
Great TA!

She's very sweet and understanding. You can skip the days that she doesn't have kahoots and quizzes, or in-class activities and she will tell you beforehand under eLC weekly sections what her lesson plan is. Take her!! She did use her own book and you have to complete a reading guide for it but you can find it for free online. Save money!

I took her Foundations of Reading class, and she's such an amazing person! She is clear and concise in her lectures. We do Kahoots at least once a week (which is a free 100). She has homework due before every class, but I've never struggled to get it done. I've never made anything less than an A on anything graded, and I've never even had to study!

Professor Sayeski is the BEST!!! I loved her class so much. It's clear that she is passionate about teaching, and she wants you to care too. The class is super easy, mainly consisting of in-class Kahoots, engaging lectures, or watching documentaries/films. I genuinely loved learning from her and hugged her on the last day of class. TAKE HER!!!!

Instructions and what is expected is extremely unclear. It is very difficult to succeed in this course because it is a guessing game as to what she wants you to say on tests. Take someone else!! She is so unsure of herself. Gives very unclear responses to questions and her test are so strange. All written and she is looking for very specific answers. He was nice, but didn't really teach. He struggled to actually teach us and will only go over a few things. Then we had to teach ourselves during class. He only really helps the ones who need it. Very light grader.

She's a very caring professor, I just didn't enjoy the linkedin learning format of the class. She'll give good feedback on your projects and is really easy to talk to. Take her class!!

THE ACTUAL GOAT! She is SO caring and teaches the content so well. Don't bother with the homework, just review the in-class problems/packets. She gives so much partial credit its hard not to do well. She is so kind and I felt that this class was so much easier than ACCT 5000. Study well for every quiz/exam and you'll do great! TAKE HER!

A challenging class, but Professor Valentine is great. She is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the class, and makes it interesting. Also, she is super approachable and genuinely cares about the class and the futures of her students.

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 117 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr.Capps is really engaging and deeply cares about student learning, but she is definitely a no-BS professor. Try to participate in class and expect work/quizzes outside of class every week (lots of readings, but you get better at them quickly), and each quiz has 2 attempts. The writings require preparation with the readings, but aren't too bad

No homework, attendence is majority of grade, easy A for a class but the professor is annoying.  She constantly boasts about how her tests are ai proof and will flip her lid if you walk in the wrong door while class is started.  Tests are graphical interpertations, like sat/act style questions so if youre not good at those you might struggle a bit

Good professor with a very lenient grading policy. She wants her students to do well and seems passionate about what she's teaching. Attendance is literally 52% of your grade so if you show up to class every day it is an easy A. Do not take her class if you plan on skipping a lot. Tests are online and open note/browser but are sort of difficult.

by textbooks i mean you have to purchase an app that uses geolocation to see if you are really in class or not. its the biggest part of her class and while she lectures you'll have to answer questions on there. for some of the questions it doesn't matter if you are right and for others it does and calculates your percentage for the day.

Over half of your grade is based off of attendance and tophat points so you do need to go to the lectures. However, Dr. Capps does really care about her students and wants you to do well in the class. If you know you are not good with attendance, do not take her classes. Otherwise, her grading is easy and as long as you show up you should do good.

OMCow!  That woman thinks the only way to act is to have someone beat you over the head with the "Method" book.  I got a bad grade in there because I don't believe in method acting.  I don't believe you have to hit yourself in the head to know what it feels like to be hit in the head!  I don't believe you have to get raped to be able to act like someone who has just been raped. ARG!!! ... I think I will digress, as she is no longer adjunct-"ing" at AC, because Scott Clark is

Mk, so, Theatre Major? I am speaking to the fact that if you've gotten to this point, you might want to release your inhibitions to the wind or your voice. This was the toughest and best acting course I've had.  If you want to pursue acting and want to be an actor, take this class.  I found it very challenging because of what we had to do.  Glad it's offered during the Maymester so I could focus on it.  I would take it again.  It was such a great class for personal discovery. It is tough. Good luck.

I had been out of school for four years working as an orderly and transporter (night-shift) at a local hospital. I was working full time when I took her class, I got a {C}. review_highlights.comment: I felt that I should respond to another rating about Prof. Kwass never giving A's.  I got A's on all of my papers and in the class overall.  I loved the challenge of the course.  The class isn't designed to easily burn one of your electives.  I loved the class, and it was by far my favorite college course that I ever took!

This is a great class if you don't mind discussion.  We had 3 papers (25% each), and the rest of the grade was discussion in class.  The readings were interesting and manageable.  He lectures for about the first 20-30 minutes, and discussion follows.  I would recommend this to anyone without a shy persona.
I had him for Enlightenment-- it was the best class I have taken at UGA.  I feel... Enlightened.  Kwass is a great guy and you won't regret taking the class.
