analysis.name: Peter Lambert-Cole
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Doesn't post HW. Lecture is really fast. Basically self-taught by doing practice from textbook and practice exams. Exams are fairly easy if you prepare well enough. 2 midterms (40%) and 1 final (30%). I'm not even sure how grades are going to be since 20% is HW, and he has never posted any, but 3/15. Rec this prof if looking for a lowkey class.

Stopped assigning homework after week two up until the last like 2 weeks of class. Didn't post anything on ELC besides practice tests which were helpful. Attendance isn't mandatory but he doesn't post notes or anything so the only way to get the information is to go to class or teach yourself.

He doesn't seem to show a lot of preparation or effort with notes and often forgets to post homework and answer keys. He is nice and seems to like the subject but it is hard to understand his explanations of things. His answer keys are very mesyy and often times incorrect so you are kind of on your own in this class.

Professor Lambert-Cole clearly has a deep passion for all things math and physics, but it doesn't translate well into teaching. He was unprepared during the entirety of the course. He never posted answer keys when he said he would, and even then, the answer keys were often riddled with mistakes. If you have him, expect to teach yourself most of it.

He's clearly passionate about math and enjoys teaching it. His examples and clarifications on topics are good but he can ramble. Stutters a lot too. He doesn't post much graded homework so the large large bulk of your grade is basically just 2 midterms and a final. He doesn't respond to emails. He does offer extra credit for the final.

analysis.name: William Lanzilotta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Starting off it can be hard to get used to his lecturing style and slideshows as they're quick and a little disorganized, but he really took the time to help students understand concepts. His quizzes are pretty much directly from the VSGs, so they were not the most difficult once you figure out how to study and I recommend going to office hours.

Teaches the first half of the course and gives weekly quizzes. Lecture slides can be a bit confusing on their own but if you pay attention and ask questions it'll make sense. He's happy to go over your quiz with you during office hours to provide feedback. Quizzes are almost entirely based off the VSG, so if you're active on that you'll do fine.

There were weekly quizzes that were kinda hard but they were derived from the VSG so it was doable. Also I thought he was an interesting lecturer and gave good feedback when I went into to review the weekly quizzes, so im not sure why so many reviews are calling him passive aggressive when I thought he was nice and just trying to help.

It's very clear that Dr. L is a researcher first. He lectures very fast and is incredibly condescending if you don't understand things the first time. I've also never had a professor be as rude as he is in emails and other communication. The only good thing about the class is that the quizzes are pretty similar to the study guide.

Dr. Lanzilotta is a great professor. His lectures are engaging and he will go back over concepts if people have trouble with them. He is available for office hours if needed for extra help. The VSG prepares you well for exams if you use it.

analysis.name: William Lastrapes
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There are more engaging and supportive professors. The class feels more advanced than needed, with too much untested detail, and slides do not match his exam style. He posts previous exams, but doing well on them may not translate to the real test and can build false confidence. Quizzes help some, but can be out of scope. Would take with diff prof.

Picked certain topics out of the book to cover. Exams had similar questions to past exams, which he posts. Long-winded explanations are boring and he doesn't have many practice materials. Interested in talking to students about economics. Passionate about specific topics which are not in book! Go to class to learn it. Use AI to explain content!

It's a decent class when you need it to graduate or for a requirement, but get ready for weekly exams that make up most of your grade, and the homework each week is also tedious. Even though it's an online class I still struggled with getting an A since so much is relied on your weekly tests

Professor did not teach the class, it was entirely virtual. This is less of a rating for him and moreso for taking Macro online. DO NOT TAKE MACRO ONLINE. It was so  hard for no reason. I'm currently taking micro irl and it is so much easier. You have to consume all 400 pages of the textbook. The final exam was heinous. I worked so hard.

This class was fairly simple (8 graded module tests, open note, that are 40% of your grade, and a final, closed note, exam worth 60% of your grade). As long as you read the textbook you should be fine, but make sure to prepare for the final, and get the best possible grade on your module tests to buffer the weight of the final.

analysis.name: Jennifer Large
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: MIST5750.I Had personal issues going on early in the semester causing me to have a LOTof missing assignment she let me do them all with a massive extension, offered extra credit for 15 percent on test , and additional 1% to final grade with evaluation and a survey at the end.Content is not hard to learn. literally saved my semester. GOAT! TAKE HER!

She was very nice and caring. You do have assignments due almost every Sunday, but they are pretty straight forward and don't require too much effort. She also has a one day late policy where you can turn in your assignment up to a day late without penalty which came in handy a lot! She does take attendance regularly, but the class was very easy!

This was Prof Large's first semester at UGA, so I can understand why her lectures were not strong. However, sometimes it felt like she didn't know the material she was teaching. But, she gives a lot of opportunities to improve your grade in the class, so that really saved my grade. Python itself isn't too bad, but the quizzes are a little tricky.

This was her first semester at UGA and you could tell. As the semester went on, she got more comfortable with everything. The material is not that hard and she is a very easy grader, but her lectures are super boring. I only went to class because I was already in the building. The assignments are a lot of work but are basically completion.

She was a pretty solid professor. Sure her lectures could be more engaging, and the tests are kind of difficult, the material is still easy to memorize for the most part, and the assignments teach you a lot and the ERPsim game you get to do is pretty fun.

analysis.name: Kyser Lough
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor, listens to feedback and clear that he cares a lot. He wants his students to do well and will adapt his class to ensure that. Includes interesting stories and case studies in his lectures and does a good job of engaging the class. He's also hilarious.

Loved JRLC3700E with Dr. Lough! He genuinely cares about his students. Lectures are broken up into easily digestible segments, and half the work is going out into the world and practicing photography using the knowledge learned in lectures. Daily photo posts, 4 reflections, daily modules, and a 3 photo "final". I 100% recommend taking this course!

I loved Lough. He made ethics such a fun class, and I looked forward to going to his class more than any other. He's super clear about what will be on tests, and we had an easy reflection to submit each week as well. His lectures were super interesting and engaging, and he even added in silly questions between slides to lighten the mood.

This was my second class with Dr. Lough, and he is still one of my favorite professors. The class was based on weekly readings, with written reflections at the end of each week, and two exams. He is such a kind and understanding professor, and he is super passionate about what he teaches. I will always recommend him to anyone!

Dr. Lough is passionate about music journalism and genuinely engages the class in discussions(very little work-load). He confirmed that I had picked the absolute best odyssey out there. The class culminates to an Athens Porchfest workshop that was extremely rewarding. Overall, definitely take this odyssey or one of his other courses. He's the best!

analysis.name: Kyle Bower
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: overall really good. actually cared about you and allowed you to ask questions in lectures.

Dr. Bower lectures ALL OF CLASS. There are theory discussions once a week which are easy A's. She does a test review before each test giving away 10-12 questions off of the test. She doubled the length of a paper 15 hours before it was due and the grading criteria did not make sense. She is kind, but the class was pretty boring.

Kyle is such a great professor, I really enjoyed being in her class. She posts the powerpoints, but she leaves out a couple slides (that can be found in the textbook). Class isn't mandatory, but I went to every class because we also watch videos that are on the test. Tests reflect the class material fairly well. Study and you'll pass!

Dr. Bower is a nice professor, but do not bother sending her emails, she never responds. There are very few assignments, but they are graded heavily. She posts everything practically online, but come on Fridays for a participation grade. If you want a professor who you can communicate with,I would not recommend.

I love this class! She has the perfect amount of assignments to make sure missing one homework will not harm your grade too badly but also its not an overwhelming amount of work. I loved this course so much and Dr. bower uses her own experiences as examples so you fully understand them

If you are up to date with the slides he is teaching you will have fun in the class lecture. review_highlights.comment: Turner is great! His tests are very straightforward and you can have a sheet of notes for each test. Overall, the class is really easy if you put any effort in at all. All of his notes are on powerpoint, so no textbooks to buy.
Mr. Turner is a great teacher. Very easy class and he really makes sure everyone understands the material. Very helpful and nice. Would definitely take this teacher again and/or recommend to others.
Mr. Turner really cares about his students. If you come to class and pay attention, you should make an A in the class.  If you can take this class instead of STAT 2000 (you probably can), do it!

I had Mr. Turner during his first semester as a college professor and he was great! The lectures were kinda boring but he did what he could to make them interesting. He was always very helpful and wanted the class to do good! As long as your pay attention you'll get an A. We had homework and labs every week but they brought up my overall average.

Professor Turner makes this class easy for you! The lectures can be boring, but as long as you do the homework and practice tests, you will be fine for the tests. I never studied because we got to use "cheat sheets" for the tests and they helped a lot. I'm taking him again for BioS 3000 and I'm glad to have him again!

Professor Woosman is a very nice guy. Easy FYOS about tourism. You just turn in about 4-5 things but no hard grading put some effort and you'll get an A. One of my favorite professors! He is a chill, humorous, and kind person. The class itself was very interesting to learn and towards the end, the class ate dinner together.

review_highlights.comment: Kyle is a great linguistics teacher, he gives homework and quizzes on elc so you can do them with your notes. Do not buy textbook, he gives page references in lectures if you want but you really don't need it. There's extra credit if you forget to do homework. Kyle changes due dates often so you have to go to class often bc he won't email.

I never thought I would enjoy a class like this but he made it great. Kyle is the best professor I have ever had! He is the total package: funny, cares about his work, easy to talk to, gives extra credit, and is all around awesome! It might say to get the current edition textbook for the class, but you can probably get the old edition and be fine.

Kyle is an amazing professor! He is passionate about the work he does and cares for his students. The class was so much fun, even at 8 am. The end of the year project seemed like it was going to be horrendous, but it actually was a ton of fun and didn't take a lot of effort to get a good grade!  Do yourself a favor & take his class!

Kyle is super easy going and a great prof. He makes a rather boring subject super enjoyable and interesting. Tests were exactly what you'd expect, no surprises & always extra credit. Caring, funny, & charismatic, he's always making class fun. He's also kinda hot too, so that's always plus

Kyle is the best professor I've had so far! His class is interesting and he is awesome. If you study the material, you will get an A for sure. I spent about an hour preparing for each test and I got a 100 on all of them. He's super laid back and friendly. I would definitely recommend him!!

analysis.name: Mark Leeper
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I don't see him on the schedule for the summer or fall--it is my understanding UGA hired other profs to teach AmGov and law courses. What a shame. UGA needs other professors like Dr. Leeper. He engages the class, answers every question, and motivates you to follow and understand American politics.

marky marky mark. self proclaimed 'communist' and 'member of the deep state' so be careful before he indoctrinates you into his wokeness, they're eating the cats and the dogs. there were about 4 assignments the whole semester, no hard due dates, no required attendance, very engaging lectures, and somehow i genuinely learned a lot. i have no idea.

Like overall chill guy who gives no work, but there's actually no reason to go to class because he just rambles. He'll send emails to show up making you feel like there is an in-class assignment or he's taking attendance, but he never does.
Professor Leeper was great! He didn't make POLS harder than it needed to be and had fun engaging lectures. Only a few written assignments throughout the semester and is really understanding.

in two years I have taken all three of his classes. they all were great, but Politics of the Supreme Court was the best class I encountered in the department-- by far.  I was sorry to hear the department is letting him go after this year--a big mistake. He is great for students aiming for law school.

Take him if you can this year.

He loves to joke around, the best part. Add headings to your papers!

Dr. Banks is so cool and fun to be around and his class was super fun! This class is discussion based and the conversations are always enjoyable. I always walked away learning something new. Few assignments that aren't hard but can't be started at the last minute either. No tests. 1000% recommend and I will definitely seek him out in the future!
A great professor and I would recommend taking any class with him!

Loved this class and Professor Leon. He's so funny and everyone was always joking and comfortable. The assignments are a bit long but easy to do if you start a bit early. Little unorganized but gives him character. Would take again if I could.

Dr. Banks is genuinely such a kind man who cares for the students he teaches. The class is very conversation-based, but it is easy to participate. Few papers throughout the semester, but all dates and guidelines are laid out in the syllabus.

Brian is A WONDERFUL PROFESSOR! He will consistently help you in class if you ask for it. It's important to attend class for a true deaf culture experience. ABSOLUTELY LOVE BRIAN! He's an amazing professor and makes the class so immersive and fun. I am actually taking AMSL 1020 with him next semester because of how much I loved him. I would definitely recommend him to anyone wanting to take ASL and learning to sighn!!

Brian is AMAZING! I wish I could take him for every ASL class. He cares about all of his students and makes sure everyone understands the content. He kindly corrects mistakes and I felt like my signing capabilities grew soooo much this year!

Easy A, two tests and cumulative final (one dropped), video assignments, and two super easy papers (easy 100). Seriously take him! He's literally my favorite professor

AMAZING professor! She took student feedback into account and really cared about the students. The pop quizzes were pretty hard, but she took our feedback and helped us perform better on them. The final consists of pop quizzes, in class assignments, attendance, a final project, and 2 exams.

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sawyer was the second professor I've take for my law minor. I didn't mind his class too much, but nobody ever seems to know what's going on (including him). The course is not easy, but it is not impossible; your TA is your best resource to succeed. No formal curve, but the TAs work together to ensure some continuity across them. Average test grade is a low to mid B

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zhang's 'Woody Plant ID' (HORT3720) course is awesome! I highly recommend taking this course if you're interested in learning more about the plants on campus and how to identify and/or differentiate similar-looking species. Lecture-heavy course with weekly plant walks around campus. Grades are 10 ID quizzes and a final.

Dr. Zhang has been my favorite professor so far. I've had him for Hort 3000 and Hort 3620, and I never leave his class in a bad mood. He's very caring and passionate about what he teaches. If you go to class every day and pay attention during lectures, you'll be golden. Midterm and final and weekly quizzes (he hints at what you need to focus on).

Super nice guy. If you want an FYOS that requires very little outside work, I'd recommend this one. Kind of long lectures but usually would let us out early. You do take a few field trips to farms but they don't take long at all. Brings tea and snacks to every class.

Plant Prop has been my favorite college course! Students go on industry tours and field trips to local companies. Expect a midterm and final exam, research paper, lab reports (field trips), etc. This class has so many opportunities for real-world application, and Dr. Zhang is an amazing lecturer! Highly recommend. Textbook is optional.

Dr. Zhang is one of the most passionate and thoughtful professors I have met at UGA. This course is a great place for anyone looking to gain basic horticultural knowledge. Expect a midterm and final exam, a research project, and pop quizzes. His class is amazing; you'll be successful if you participate and review lectures.
